study.question: Can a norm-preserving nonlinear completion basis improve the failed parameter-matched linear completion of15-dimensional item tables, while preserving stronger-source click AUC and reducing measured prediction cost?
study.hypothesis: Observed: source/full16 clickAUC0.660646940486458; native coupled15 0.6605886110435017; zero-lift15 and masked16 both0.6605479438111359. Latest learned linear completion0.6604963319130357 loses0.0000516118981002 to frozen/zero completion and0.0001506085734223 to full16; it did not solve retention. A linear appended coordinate remains in the affine span of15 lookup coordinates. An absolute-value basis can supply a nonlinear coordinate from those same permitted inputs, with identical90 learned coefficients and equal completion-input norm. It may supply useful sign-insensitive information without another per-ID table coordinate. This is a provisional function-class hypothesis, not an explanation established by previous results or a missing-coordinate reconstruction claim.

study.proposed_difference: In _lift_item feed embedded[..., :15].abs() into the existing coordinate_completion row; leave the first15 coordinates untouched. This single operator maps each field independently before history compression and target extraction. Absolute value preserves per-vector L2 norm and zeros, but can increase the affine rank of the16-dimensional lifted outputs without increasing free per-ID lookup dimension. It supplies no new sample information, no cross-field reconstruction, no supervised reconstruction label and no guarantee of restoring the deleted source coordinate. Pair against byte-identical prior linear source, an identical frozen absolute map, and byte-identical full16 source. This is an empirical replacement study; novelty is unverified.
predictions: At initialization candidate/linear/frozen-absolute predictions and inherited buffers should match zero-lift under identical inputs, mode and state; no constructor RNG consumption is added.
If nonlinear completion is useful, absolute_completion15 improves validation click AUC over both linear_completion15_replay and frozen_absolute15 at identical persistent parameter count.
Frozen absolute should remain at zero completion and reproduce zero-lift active outputs/gradients within declared numerical tolerance; any score change needs investigation.

For six independent tables, candidate and linear have30544234 parameters,30276907 embedding and267327 dense; frozen absolute has the same persistent count but90 fewer trainable parameters. Relative to full16 this saves1516219 parameters (about4.73%); host counts override inference.
Whether the new abs/matmul path is faster than full16 is uncertain. Efficiency requires measured p50/p95 and throughput rather than parameter savings alone.
falsifiers: No positive click delta over both linear and frozen absolute defeats the proposed useful nonlinear replacement in this setting.
Remaining clickAUC below full16 defeats exact quality preservation; no post-hoc noninferiority margin will convert a loss into success.
No smaller measured parameter count or no measured inference cost improvement defeats the combined efficiency claim, even if AUC rises.
Failed initialization, masking, ownership or forward/backward gates invalidate causal interpretation as an implementation issue; retain costs and do not label that scientific refutation.
Any benefit depending on unauthorized inputs, auxiliary gradient leakage or modified host recipe is inadmissible.
alternative_explanations: Different nonlinear gradients may change the single-pass optimizer trajectory without recovering useful compressed information; the function-class and optimizer effects are not fully separable here.
Appended absolute features can encode embedding magnitude and shift scorer/tower statistics; a gain does not identify the deleted-coordinate semantics.
A loss from the previous linear map could arise from single-seed optimization or AdamW/Adagrad interaction rather than insufficient expressiveness.

Prior width/allocation changes are not monotonic: coupled8 achieved0.6599120831369636, coupled14 0.660482133621223, native14 was worse, suffix/interior drops lost versus prefix15 and asymmetric reductions lost versus uniform15. These trajectories constrain conclusions but do not prove coordinate redundancy.
Native15 and zero-lift15 differed by0.0000406672323658 despite related representational capacity; BF16 kernels/layout and optimization are credible confounds.

Inference timing varies across identical replays; a small apparent speedup may be noise. Existing trials have no requested candidate diagnostics and supply no independent-seed or user-cluster confidence estimates.
